subject: math
title: Unit A · Probability — Unit Quiz
source: authored (math is guided-lesson content, not module.js)

questions.prompt: A fair 10-sided die. What is the probability of rolling a 7, written as a percent? (whole number)
On a fair 6-sided die, what is the probability of rolling an even number?
questions.explain: Three faces are even (2, 4, 6) out of six → 3/6 = 1/2.

questions.prompt: You roll two 6-sided dice. How many equally-likely outcomes are there in all?
questions.explain: 6 × 6 = 36 (each of die A's 6 outcomes pairs with die B's 6).

questions.prompt: What is the probability of rolling the exact pair (2, 2) with two dice?
questions.explain: One square out of the 36 equally-likely ones → 1/36.

questions.prompt: With two dice, how many different (ordered) ways can you roll a sum of 5?
Which total is the MOST likely when rolling two dice?
questions.explain: 7 has the most ways to make it (6 of them) → 6/36 = 1/6.

questions.prompt: When counting the ways to make a sum, (2,5) and (5,2) count as the same outcome.
questions.explain: They are two different rolls (order matters), so we count both.

questions.prompt: On a fair die, what is the probability of NOT rolling a 6?
Flip 3 coins. What is the probability of getting AT LEAST ONE Heads?
questions.explain: 1 − P(no Heads) = 1 − 1/8 = 7/8 (only TTT has no Heads).

questions.prompt: How many ways are there to get exactly 2 Heads in 4 coin flips? (that's C(4,2))
questions.explain: C(4,2) = 6 — the middle number of row 4 of Pascal's triangle.

questions.prompt: A bag has 3 red and 2 blue marbles. You draw one red and KEEP it. What is the probability the next marble is also red?
questions.explain: After removing a red, 2 red remain of 4 marbles → 2/4 = 1/2 (the bag changed).

questions.prompt: In the Monty Hall game, what is your probability of winning the car if you ALWAYS switch?
questions.explain: Switching wins in 2 of the 3 equally-likely cases → 2/3.

questions.prompt: In your own words, explain why a total of 7 is more likely than a total of 2 when you roll two dice.
questions.rubric: Full marks: the answer says probability = (ways to make the total) ÷ 36 (or 'favourable outcomes ÷ total'), and that 7 has more ways/combinations (six: 1+6, 2+5, 3+4, 4+3, 5+2, 6+1) while 2 has only one way (1+1). Partial: mentions 7 has more combinations but doesn't tie it to counting out of 36. Award 0 if it only says '7 is lucky' or gives no counting reason.
questions.explain: P(sum) = (ways to make it) ÷ 36. Seven has 6 ways; two has only 1 (1+1). More ways → more likely.

questions.prompt: Explain, in your own words, why switching doors wins about 2/3 of the time in the Monty Hall problem.
questions.rubric: Full marks: notes that the first pick is right only 1/3 of the time, so 2/3 of the time the car is behind one of the other doors; the host then opens the goat among those, concentrating that 2/3 onto the single remaining door, so switching wins 2/3. Partial: says switching wins 2/3 and staying 1/3 without the 'first pick is 1/3' reasoning, or enumerates the 3 cases correctly. Award 0 for '50/50' or no reasoning.
questions.explain: Your first pick is right 1/3 of the time; the other 2/3 gets concentrated onto the one door you can switch to.
